newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung to report choice of officials to Beijing.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung to report choice of officials to Beijing.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Monday he would travel to Beijing this week to report to China's leaders on his choice of top mandarins to serve as policy secretaries after the handover later this year.
His office said in a statement Tung would "nominate and report to the Central People's government" on Wednesday and return from Beijing on Thursday.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

The outgoing British colonial administration has urged Tung to make as few changes as possible in the ranks of top civil servants who hold positions akin to cabinet ministers in Britain and wield considerable power.

Tung won public aclaim when he invited Hong Kong's popular Chief Secretary Anson Chan, head of the civil service and deputy to British governor Chris Patten, to stay on, guaranteeing continuity in uncertain times.
She accepted, but the fate of her senior policy secretaries remains to be decided.
Tung named his inner circle of advisers, or Executive Council, last month.
The list included two members who currently serve on the colonial Governor's Executive Council.

He also followed the practice of the outgoing British administration of reserving slots on his Executive Council for Hong Kong's top three civil servants -- currently the Chief Secretary, the Attorney General and the Financial Secretary.
